title: Fourier coefficients under coordinate flips
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $S,T\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. If $x^S$ denotes the vector obtained by flipping the coordinates in $S$, then the Fourier coefficient at $T$ of the function $x\mapsto f(x^S)$ equals $(-1)^{|T\cap S|}\widehat f(T)$, where Fourier coefficients are taken with respect to the uniform measure on the Boolean cube.
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. For $S\subseteq[n]$, let $x^S$ be the bit vector obtained by flipping exactly the coordinates in $S$. For every real cube function $f$ and sets $S,T\subseteq[n]$, $\widehat{(x\mapsto f(x^S))}(T)=(-1)^{|T\cap S|}\widehat f(T)$.
